method: Average-linkage hierarchical clustering of the 29 root topics. Distance between topics a and b = 1 - cosine similarity of their link profiles, where a topic's profile is the symmetrised, row-normalised matrix of topic-to-topic hyperlink counts in the full core link graph (profile entries for a and b themselves removed). Two topics are close when the pages in them link to the same other topics. Chosen because it depends only on the Wikipedia link structure and page topic labels, not on any run, model or reader.
notes: Clustering input: hyperlink connectivity between the 29 root topics in the full enwiki-20260901 core link graph (224.6M edges; 6.6M pages); no run, model or reader data is used, so animating runs over the tree is not circular.

Each page has one primary topic = the root topic with the largest weight in the page-topic table (agrees with the layout topic on 0.9999 of the 12,586 layout pages). 11533 of those 12586 layout pages belong to more than one topic; they count only for their primary topic in paths and flows.

39 layout pages have no topic (layout topic -1); they appear as leaf id -1 in topic_paths.json and are excluded from mass shares and flows (treated as missing). Consequence: the start page 0-6-0 has no topic, so all flows out of it are dropped (agents and readers); readers flows also lose one ING Group target (Inter-Alpha Group of Banks), so reader flows sum to about 18.8 start-weights, not 20.

Robustness: cophenetic correlation of this tree with a tree from direct link lift is 0.17 and with a tree from page co-membership overlap (Jaccard) 0.22; fit of the tree to its own distances (cophenetic corr) 0.86. The agreement between the three trees is LOW: read the dendrogram as one reasonable ordering of topics, not as a finding about topic kinship.

Agents mass = share of arrivals over all replay runs of the 8 models (the 10 GPT-4.1 runs are in topic_paths.json with model key GPT4.1 but not in mass or flows, as in the terrain data; all conditions, all steps; path[1:] for hub starts, path[0:] for blank-page runs); runs are not weighted equally by model. Per-model mass uses the same rule.

Readers mass and flows are STEP 1 ONLY: the top-15 listed clicks per start (Wikimedia clickstream), renormalised per start, equal start weights, 20 starts; flows from_leaf is the start page topic. Units are start-weighted shares (sum = 20), not click counts. Nothing is known about readers beyond the first click.
Flows include same-topic transitions (from == to); agents: consecutive distinct pages in a run path, all steps; counts are traversals.

Subtopics come from a category tree (category icicle: BFS from the 29 root categories; pages count in every category they belong to; agent_visits = visits to the 12.6k layout pages in that category, reader_clicks = clickstream inbound clicks to those pages). The category tree is noisy and counts overlap, so n_pages differs from the primary-topic n_pages in leaves. Top 5 by n_pages.

Round-1 figure 'Humans topic 16.0% of clicks vs 7.0% of visits' is from the icicle totals (all inbound clickstream clicks to layout pages vs agent visits), recomputed here from the category tree as 16.0% vs 7.0%. It is NOT comparable to readers mass here, which is step-1 clicks from 20 starts.

first = topic of the FIRST click only, per start (20 hub starts, blank-page runs excluded), equal start weights, all conditions; comparable with readers mass, which is also first clicks. Used for the bars on the Topics page.

link_counts_topic_by_topic.note: rows = from topic, cols = to topic, ids 0..28, full core graph
